open_questions.question: Does true long-range orientational order remain absent at the full paper scale (up to 1000 sites, square/rectangular AND circular patches)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Our 151-site circular patch already shows decaying correlations, but finite-size effects can mask weak LRO; the paper's key claim is scale-robust absence of LRO.
open_questions.next_step: Regenerate patches of N=300,600,1000 in multiple shapes and check that C(r) and the orientation structure factor do not sharpen with N.

open_questions.question: Do the odd-parity ground states quantitatively reproduce the decagonal HBS tiling geometry (hexagon+boat+star decomposition), not just its statistical fingerprints?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's central visual is the HBS superstructure outlined by thin-rhombus short-diagonal pairs/triplets; matching it geometrically is stronger evidence than histograms.
open_questions.next_step: Identify thin-rhombus short diagonals from the pentagrid tiles, tag pair/triplet chains, and overlay the HBS decomposition on the relaxed configuration.

open_questions.question: Is the observed lack of LRO purely a frustration effect of the interaction Hamiltonian, or partly geometric to the tiling?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper notes an ordered arrow arrangement DOES exist geometrically (Lifshitz; Cockayne-Widom edge model); disentangling energetic vs geometric frustration guides Hamiltonian design for order.
open_questions.next_step: Compare our vertex-based rotor ground state against the Cockayne-Widom edge-arrow model energy on the same tiling to see which Hamiltonian admits LRO.

open_questions.question: How does the critical interparticle separation R_c (maximal short-range order) emerge when dipolar and octopolar contributions are combined with realistic 1s-2s ratios?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper predicts an optimal R_c ~ 1s-2s where SRO is maximal; this controls real nanomagnet/adsorbate design.
open_questions.next_step: Add mixed l=1+l=3 couplings with a tunable size parameter s and scan R_c by locating the peak of the nearest-neighbour correlation.

open_questions.question: Do the even-parity multipoles (l=2 quadrupole, l=4 hexadecapole) show the predicted 90-degree / 72-degree local alignment and weaker, harder-to-quantify SRO?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Completes the parity dichotomy that is the paper's organizing theme; even-parity is the harder analysis case.
open_questions.next_step: Extend the rotor kernel with even-parity angular potentials (double-headed arrows, head-to-center attraction) and measure nearest-neighbour angle histograms.

next_steps: Finite-size scaling of correlations and structure factor to N=1000.
